--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.select_nodes_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select nodes by their IDs. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.select_nodes_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select nodes by their IDs. title: >- [Graph.select_nodes_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Select nodes by their IDs. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select nodes by their IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23273-L23383){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.select_nodes_by_id( node_ids, set_op="union", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select nodes by id](../assets/graphs/select-nodes-by-id.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Six nodes labeled by their integer ids 1 to 6. After select_nodes_by_id with ids 1, 3, and 5, those three nodes are selected and drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Selects the given nodes. This is the most direct way to build a selection when you already know which nodes you want, for example from the output of an analysis method (`get_non_neighbors()`, a community, a shortest path) or from a filtered node DataFrame. Common uses: - turning the result of a query that returns node IDs into a selection for `*_ws` methods such as `set_node_attrs_ws()` or `transform_to_subgraph_ws()` - seeding a traversal with `trav_out()`, `trav_in()`, or `trav_both()` - re-applying a selection that was saved earlier with `get_selected_node_ids()` The nodes are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise, and duplicate IDs are ignored. Only integer IDs are accepted; to select by label, convert with `get_id_from_label()` or use `select_nodes(lambda n: n.label in {...})`. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer node IDs to select. Every ID must belong to an existing node; a missing ID raises `KeyError` and leaves the selection unchanged. Strings (labels) are rejected with a `TypeError`. An empty list is allowed (with `set_op="replace"`, it clears the selection). [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How these nodes combine with the current node selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected nodes among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. Any edge selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NodeNotFoundError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any node ID doesn't exist in the graph (a subclass of both `KeyError` and `ValueError`). [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `node_ids=` contains a non-integer such as a label. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting nodes by ID marks them for follow-up operations like building a subgraph. `get_selected_node_ids()` reports back the same IDs that were selected: ::: {#45a866b7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) id_a = graph.get_id_from_label("A") id_b = graph.get_id_from_label("B") graph.select_nodes_by_id([id_a, id_b]) sorted(graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2] ``` ::: ::: Selecting "C" afterwards adds it to the selection, which grows to all three nodes. `transform_to_subgraph_ws()` could then keep exactly these nodes: ::: {#c8f311cc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_nodes_by_id([graph.get_id_from_label("C")]) graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A typical pattern is to turn the output of an analysis into a selection. Here the nodes not adjacent to "A" are selected and tagged as link-prediction candidates: ::: {#97799da4 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) ( graph .select_nodes_by_id(graph.get_non_neighbors("A")) .set_node_attrs_ws(candidate=True) .get_node_df() .select("label", "candidate") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
